title: Reflection of local finite presentations across surjective closed immersions
statement: Let p:V→U be a surjective closed immersion of schemes, R a monoid object in abelian pro-etale sheaves on U, and M an R-module sheaf. If p* M is locally finitely presented over p* R (a pro-etale covering with finite free cokernel presentations), then M is locally finitely presented over R. This is a reflection statement; no noetherianity, reducedness or uniform nilpotence bound is assumed.

proof.text: A surjective closed immersion is a universal homeomorphism. Compute topological invariance as in Lemma 5.4.2 using the affine ind-etale basis of Theorem 2.3.4. Base change on that basis is an equivalence preserving faithfully flat and Zariski covering criteria. Refine the finite presentation covering of p* M to basis objects and lift this refined covering. The induced monoidal sheaf equivalence agrees with the closed inverse-image adjunction.

The monoidal sheaf equivalence identifies the coefficient rings and regular modules, and preserves finite sums and cokernels. Transport the finite matrices and their cokernel isomorphisms to the lifted covering of U. Compatibility with the adjunction unit identifies these cokernels with the original M. Empty U uses the empty cover and rank-zero presentations.
